# hwatu

> Headless verification browser for AI coding agents: daemon-based WebKitGTK, real rendering, ~13ms median window spawn, ~35ms one-call verify pass (`hwatu check`)

hwatu is AI-first: the primary user is a coding agent verifying web
UIs in its inner loop, headlessly, without stealing focus. Jcode
drives it natively as its `browser` backend; other integrations are a
one-line JSON protocol over a Unix socket, a CLI mirroring it, and
`hwatu mcp`, a Model Context Protocol server over stdio for Claude
Code, Cursor, and other MCP clients. Agent-facing tools: `check`
(open+load+eval+screenshot+diff+close in one call), `verify`
(repo-level contract with preflight, dev server, viewport sweep,
evidence report), pixel `diff` with match percent and significant
regions, `snapshot`/`click`/`type`/`expect`/`console`/`net`
automation, `motion`/`seek`/`clock` for animations as numbers, file
upload, full-page screenshots, and safe CAPTCHA/anti-bot challenge
hand-off via `hwatu challenge --wait` for manual user resolution.
hwatu detects and waits for challenges; it does not provide automatic
CAPTCHA bypass, solver API integration, token injection, or
fingerprint stealth.

The human side serves the hand-off: `hwatu focus <id>` materializes an
agent's live headless session as a normal window in the user's tiling
WM, so a person can solve a challenge or inspect a page, then the
agent resumes the same session. The human side is also a credible
primary browser for tiling WMs (Hyprland, sway, niri), which makes the
hand-off land in a window that behaves like every other window,
while intentionally excluding tabs, sync, an extension platform, and
a password store of its own.
